restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Sections 8 and 18 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098, and t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are skipped. Members are those of the winner sub-class (proof.md 18.1): phase (b, u, v) = (1, 0, 1) of the class of eta, e1 = 070c0307 + (W AND f8107cf8), uniform on 2^16 values, y = e1 - Y3. Only proposals that pass the exact fourteen-outcome filter (share 1,520,837,058,143 / 2^48) are searched further, by the guarded joint solver of proof.md 9.4, which lists every E3 root and checks all three full-word equations; by Lemma F a rejected proposal holds no counted success. Heuristic part: B = 52,256,980,094,639,195,695,325 proposals (2^75.468) of 2^21 trials succeed with probability at least 0.3919693 under H1prime-winner-rate and H4prime-winner-pass-budget, with no dependence premise: the no-hit bound uses the proved cap Zwin <= 72 (Lemma CV; proof.md 18.5).

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) per unit, 64 registers, constants as immediates (proof.md Section 11). A batch of seven packed proposal lanes costs 640 (J7 = 7,465,282,870,662,742,242,190 batches, the last charged in full); a passing lane 512 plus the proved pointwise cap 56,096 of the joint solver and root checks; a once-only set-up 269,484,072. The run halts with failure when more than L = 299,996,468,082,244,789,290 lanes pass; L + 1 are charged. N = 21,759,981,102,423,868,336,670,600 machine units; with the selection procedure charged in full, T <= (N + 8,918,253,162,100,551,680) / 430 + 2^38, log2 T = 75.4216874, checked in integers (proof.md 18.7). No sorting, no lookup by value, no table that grows with the trials.

Randomized by fresh uniform input bits: seven 32-bit words and a member field per lane, lanes made of disjoint bits (proof.md Lemmas PL and PLw). Success holds only under H1prime-winner-rate and H4prime-winner-pass-budget and is not measured. The organizer-run experiments and the submitted program are those of entry 26ebba63: they run the root instance of the construction (counter 0, flags 11) and the sub-class search of that entry. The program does not run the winner path (no winner member, fourteen-outcome filter, guarded solver or packed proposals), and no digest experiment can show the half-collision of a non-root chunk. The solver cap and the packing are proved allowances (GPT Sol 6.1, answers AR and AQ), not an implementation; no run of the winner search of any size has been made. No full 2-round collision is exhibited.

The six constants, eta, the beta* cube, the fourteen filter values and the winner phase (124 bytes of advice with the root-instance words) are the output of the selection procedure of proof.md 18.6: SEL of Section 12 plus one count of the eight phases, the largest part chosen, (1, 0, 1) over the equal (1, 1, 0) by lexicographic order. Its bound, 8,918,253,162,100,551,680 operations (below 2^54.2033 units), holds by construction and is included in time_log2; that it returns these values rests on participant records, GPT Sol's phase cells and a stated, unproved operation-rate bridge. preprocessing_log2 55 bounds it. memory_log2_bytes 44 covers the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the code, the selection and the search, all held at once. No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical, winner-specific (proof.md 18.5). Over the run's B = 52,256,980,094,639,195,695,325 independent retained proposals of the winner sub-class (proof.md 18.1, Lemma PLw), let Zwin be the number of valid trials (t != 0) of one proposal that complete the collision with an E1 outcome among the fourteen of beta*, counted over all of Q* whether or not the proposal passes the filter. Rate: E[Zwin] >= mu = (2^21 - 1) * 5 * 9297 / (7 * 2^104), five sevenths (margin 1.4) of the exact model rate pwin = 9297 / 2^104 per trial. This is the whole premise; it states no dependence clause. The no-hit bound is derived from it: Zwin <= 72 (Lemma CV) gives Pr(Zwin > 0) >= E[Zwin] / 72 (Lemma S8 with b = 1/72), so over independent proposals no hit has probability at most exp(-B * mu / 72) <= exp(-1/2) + 0.001, B being the least integer with this property (proof.md 18.3). The premise is on the winner law only, not on the law of the class or of entry 26ebba63; no premise on a mean of work or on groups of proposals is made.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 18: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, E1.c1 drawn from the cube of beta* = 18b0e098, the member e1 = 070c0307 + (W AND f8107cf8) of phase (1, 0, 1) and y = e1 - Y3, seven proposal lanes per batch from disjoint fresh input bits, t solved per trial and t = 0 skipped; Zwin counts all of Q* in every proposal.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the exact count of the winner phase (proof.md 18.4): the cells of the parity certificate (P*) by phase (GPT Sol, answer AR 1; the winner phase recounted by a helper agent of the participant with the counting program of Section 17) give the part 76,161,024 = 9297 * 2^13 on the scale 2^80, so pwin = 2^11 * 76,161,024 * 2^-128 = 9297 / 2^104 under the seven-word model, conditioned on the cube by Lemma S1 (which holds for any fixed set of members), taken at five sevenths. The lanes have disjoint inputs and each has the ordinary winner law exactly (Lemma PLw), so the packing adds no dependence. Participant evidence of Section 13 (real 32-bit counter trials matching the model on measurable partial events; a reduced-width end-to-end run) concerns the class and the sub-class of entry 26ebba63 and is untrusted by the harness; no measurement of the winner sub-class is claimed. The joint event, about 2^-91.3 per trial at the premised rate, is not measured at 32 bits.
heuristics.limitations: The rate, the factor five sevenths of pwin, is assumed; it has not been measured on the winner sub-class. No dependence clause is assumed: the no-hit bound uses only the proved cap Zwin <= 72 (rho_w <= 71, b = 1/72 in Lemma S8), which needs 71.76 times the proposals of a run priced with weak dependence (proof.md 18.9). History: entry afbe2154 (69.2566) declared this premise as H1prime-winner-rate-and-dependence, with a part (ii) sufficient when rho_w <= 0.0065; it was ruled not_evaluable on 2026-10-09, all four review lanes rating that premise unsupported (proof.md 18.9). The organizer-run experiments run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) and measure neither the rate nor the counter half-collision. No run of the winner search of any size has been made, and no measurement on the winner sub-class exists.

heuristics.statement: Supporting, winner-specific (proof.md 18.5). With probability at least 0.9995 over the coins, at most L = ceil(17 * B * pi14 / 16) = 299,996,468,082,244,789,290 of the B retained proposals pass the filter of the fourteen outcomes (pi14 = 1,520,837,058,143 / 2^48, about 2^-7.532), so the pass-count halt is not reached. Reaching it halts the run with failure; the time bound charges L + 1 passing lanes and does not depend on this premise.
heuristics.scope: The fourteen-outcome filter of proof.md Section 8 on the B retained proposal lanes of proof.md 18.3, with members of the winner sub-class: the number of passing proposals, binomial with B independent steps (Lemma PLw) and the sampler's pass probability.
heuristics.extrapolation: pi14 is the exact share for independent uniform pairs (Y9, Y3 + Y4 + w8), with a certificate in proof.md Section 8. If the sampler's pass probability is at most 1.06 pi14, the Chernoff bound puts more than L passing proposals below exp(-10^13). The product-model share alone is not a proof of this premise (GPT Sol, answer AN 7.2). A participant walk of real outer steps of the class with this filter measured 2^-7.5324 against 2^-7.5320 (proof.md 10.3; untrusted by the harness), with members from a part of the class.
heuristics.limitations: That the sampler's pass share is at most 1.06 pi14 is not proved, and it has not been measured on the winner sub-class. The time bound and the exactness of the filter do not depend on it.
